candidates.rationale: Donations: TS_MEAN($return,10) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's momentum leg, taken bare -- A's own CS_RANK(TS_MEAN(...)) wrapper is 4 nodes so isn't reused whole). TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's liquidity leg, detached from B's own CS_RANK(TS_RANK(...)) wrapper for the same reason). Fusion: multiplies raw 10-day momentum by liquidity percentile before ranking once, so momentum is scaled up in heavily-traded names and toward zero in thin ones -- a liquidity-conditioned momentum test. A has no liquidity dimension (it only spreads value against momentum); B has no momentum content at all (its second leg is a static liquidity percentile, never crossed with price change).

Donations: TS_MIN($low,21) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's support-level normaliser, detached from A's own eps-yield numerator and epsilon guard, a 7-node piece not reused whole). TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's liquidity leg, stripped of B's CS_RANK wrapper). Fusion: rebuilds the 21-day low as a close-relative support ratio (not A's earnings-yield denominator) and weights it by B's liquidity percentile -- tests whether proximity to the recent floor is a stronger signal in currently liquid names. A never looks at price location without dividing earnings into it; B has no low/support reference at all, only a high-breakdown term.

Donations: TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's liquidity leg, detached from A's own CS_RANK(TS_RANK(...)) pairing). TS_MIN($low,21) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's floor reference, taken bare -- B's own numerator subtracts it from $close, a 5-node piece not reused whole). Fusion: spans today's high down to the stock's own 21-day floor (a support-cushion width A never computes, since A only compares close to the 21-day high) and scales that cushion by liquidity turnover, which B's own range-position ratio never incorporates. Distinct from both parents' close-anchored constructions.

Donations: TS_MIN($low,21)-sibling TS_MAX($high,21) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's ceiling reference, taken bare -- A's own TS_MAX(...)-TS_MIN(...) denominator is 7 nodes, not reused whole). SUB($high,$low) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's day-range piece, taken bare -- B's own TS_STD($high-$low,10) wrapper is 5 nodes, not reused whole). Fusion: today's raw high-low range is rescaled by the stock's own 21-day high instead of B's rolling STD of the range, so a wide range reads differently for a name near its ceiling than one far below it. B only ever uses the day's range inside a volatility statistic, never as a plain level; A never looks at the current day's range at all, only the close's position over 21 days.

Donations: TS_MIN($low,21) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's floor reference, taken bare -- A's construction embeds it in both numerator and denominator, each a larger piece, not reused whole). TS_MEAN($return,21) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's momentum leg, detached from B's own sign-flip and CS_RANK wrapper, a 5-node piece not reused whole). Fusion: keeps B's asset_turnover quality gate but replaces B's return-only reversal leg with a support-cushion ratio (21-day low relative to the current high, a level A never expresses this way) minus that same momentum -- asks whether efficient firms sitting on a wide support cushion, net of how much they've already moved, behave differently. A has no fundamental gate; B has no price-level information at all.

Donations: SUB($high,$close) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's reversal-gap numerator, detached from A's own TS_STD($high-$low,10) volatility scaling, a 5-node piece not reused whole). TS_MEAN($return,21) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's momentum leg, detached from B's sign-flip and CS_RANK wrapper). Fusion: rescales A's intraday reversal gap as a fraction of price instead of A's own volatility-relative scaling, subtracts 21-day momentum, and gates the whole spread by B's asset_turnover -- tests whether a same-day high-to-close pullback net of trend means something different in operationally efficient firms. A has no fundamental content; B never uses intraday high/close information, only a smoothed daily return.

Donations: TS_MEAN($return,21) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's momentum leg, detached from A's sign-flip and CS_RANK wrapper). TS_MAX($volume,21) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's ceiling reference, taken bare -- B's own numerator/denominator pairing with $volume and TS_MIN is a larger piece, not reused whole). Fusion: keeps A's asset_turnover gate but replaces A's return-only reversal leg with a volume-exhaustion ratio (today's volume relative to its own 21-day peak, the inverse framing of B's floor-to-ceiling position) minus momentum -- asks whether efficient firms whose volume has pulled back from a recent surge show a different reversal pattern. A never looks at volume; B has no fundamental gate and no return content.

Donations: TS_MIN($volume,21) verbatim from A (3 nodes, A's floor reference, taken bare -- A's own numerator/denominator pairing with $volume and TS_MAX is a larger piece, not reused whole). TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21) verbatim from B (3 nodes, B's liquidity-percentile leg, detached from B's own price-drift subtraction). Fusion: keeps B's ROE gate and liquidity-percentile leg, but replaces B's price-drift leg (TS_DELTA($open,5)) with A's own volume-floor concept, recast as current volume's proximity to its 21-day minimum -- tests whether the liquidity-rank signal in profitable firms is confounded by volume merely sitting near its normal floor rather than genuinely elevated. B never references volume's own trailing range, only a cross-sectional rank; A has no fundamental or cross-sectional dimension.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes

with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
